fact_en:
What makes something a planet?

In 2006, the IAU set three rules: it must orbit the Sun, have enough gravity to be round (hydrostatic equilibrium), and have 'cleared' its orbit of other bodies. Pluto fails the third rule!
fact_bis:
Unsay nahimo nga planeta sa usa ka butang?

Niadtong 2006, nagbutang ang IAU og tulo ka lagda: kinahanglan maglibot sa Adlaw, adunay igo nga gravity aron manghikog (hydrostatic equilibrium), ug 'gipaalis' na ang iyang orbit sa ubang lawas. Ang Pluto wala makatagbaw sa ikatulong lagda!

findings.note: Body: "adunay igo nga gravity aron manghikog (hydrostatic equilibrium)". English is "have enough gravity to be round". "Manghikog" in Cebuano means TO COMMIT SUICIDE / hang oneself — not "to become round" (lingin/bilog). The card never says round anywhere; the only remaining hint is the untranslated English jargon "hydrostatic equilibrium", which a grade-5 reader cannot decode. So rule 2 of the IAU planet definition is unrecoverable from the Cebuano, and the sentence additionally reads as self-harm content in a children's card.

fact_en: Jupiter's colorful stripes come from its cloud layers! The light 'zones' are high, cold clouds made of ammonia crystals, while the dark 'belts' are lower, warmer regions deeper in the atmosphere.
fact_bis: Ang makulay nga guhit sa Jupiter gikan sa iyang mga cloud layer! Ang hayag nga 'zones' taas ug bugnaw nga mga panganod nga gihimo sa ammonia crystals, samtang ang ngitngit nga 'belts' mas ubos ug mas init nga mga rehiyon.

findings.note: title_bis "Mga Labay sa Jupiter" for "Jupiter's Bands". Cebuano "labay" = to throw / to pass by (Tagalog: a skein of yarn) — it is not a stripe or band. The card's OWN body uses the correct word: "Ang makulay nga guhit sa Jupiter" — strong evidence the title is the outlier, and the title as a standalone label names a different thing.

fact_en:
Did you know Pluto wasn't always our farthest planet?

Before 2006, Pluto was counted as the ninth and farthest planet from the Sun!
fact_bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga dili kanunay pinakalayo ang Pluto?

Sa wala pa ang 2006, giisip ang Pluto isip ikasiyam ug kinalayong planeta gikan sa Adlaw!

findings.note: title_bis reads "Plato Ika-siyam Bago 2006" — the card is about PLUTO, but the Cebuano title names "Plato", which in this very corpus is the word for a tectonic/dinner PLATE (12 other bis titles: "Lithosphere Plato", "Subduction Plato", "Pagduso sa mga Plato", "Ceramic sa Plato ug Tasa"). Provable bis-only corruption: the tl title of the same card is correct ("Pluto, Ika-siyam Bago 2006") and the card's own Cebuano body says "Pluto" twice, so the title is the outlier. A child browsing the feed by title is told a plate was the ninth planet before 2006; the fact is only recoverable after opening the card.

fact_en:
Did you know Charon is huge compared to Pluto?

Charon is about half the size of Pluto! This makes it the absolute largest moon compared to its planet.
fact_bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga dako kaayo ang Charon kompara sa Pluto?

Ang Charon mga katunga sa gidak-on sa Pluto! Mao nga kini ang kinadak-ang bulan kompara sa iyang planeta.

findings.note: title_en "Charon, Half of Pluto" -> title_bis "Charon, Kalimot sa Pluto". "Kalimot" is forgetting/forgetfulness (root limot), not "half" (katunga). The card's OWN body uses the correct word ("Ang Charon mga katunga sa gidak-on sa Pluto"), so the title is the outlier: it names a different thing and states nothing about size.

fact_en:
When did Voyager 1 launch?

The space probe Voyager 1 was officially launched into space in the year 1977!
fact_bis:
Kanus-a gilunsad ang Voyager 1?

Ang space probe nga Voyager 1 gilunsad sa kalawakan sa tuig 1977!

findings.note: title_en "Voyager 1 Launch" -> title_bis "Paglusad: Voyager 1". Cebuano "lusad" = to go down / alight / disembark - the opposite direction from a launch, which is "lunsad". The card's own body uses the correct form twice ("Kanus-a gilunsad...", "gilunsad sa kalawakan sa tuig 1977"), confirming the title is the outlier and a direction reversal, not a regional variant.

fact_en:
How long is a lunar day?

A full tide cycle, called a lunar day, lasts about 24 hours and 50 minutes!
fact_bis:
Unsa kadugay ang usa ka lunar day?

Ang tibuok siklo sa taob, nga gitawag og lunar day, molungtad og mga 24 ka oras ug 50 ka minuto!

findings.note: title_en "Length of a Lunar Day" -> title_bis "Gabii sa Lunar Day". "Gabii" is NIGHT, not length/duration (gidugayon/kadugayon). The body asks and answers duration correctly ("Unsa kadugay... molungtad og mga 24 ka oras ug 50 ka minuto"), so the title alone asserts a different thing - a child scanning titles reads "night of a lunar day", which is a distinct (and wrong) concept from the 24h50m cycle length.

fact_en:
Is a spring tide about the season spring?

Nope! A spring tide has nothing to do with the season. It happens twice a month when water seems to "spring up"!
fact_bis:
Bahin ba sa tingpamulak ang spring tide?

Dili! Ang spring tide walay kalambigitan sa tingpamulak. Mahitabo kini kaduha kada bulan kon ang tubig morag "motumaw" pataas!

findings.note: title_en "Spring Tide Isn't Spring" -> title_bis "Spring Tide Dili Tag". The title is cut off mid-word: "Dili Tag" denies nothing - "Tag" is a dangling prefix (tag-init / tag-ulan / tingpamulak). The body names the season correctly ("Bahin ba sa tingpamulak...", "walay kalambigitan sa tingpamulak"), so the title dropped the very term the card exists to deny.

fact_en:
What are the New Seven Wonders of the World?

They are the Great Wall of China, Petra, the Colosseum, the Taj Mahal, Machu Picchu, Christ the Redeemer, and Chichen Itza!
fact_bis:
Unsa ang mga Bag-ong Pito ka Kahibulongan sa Kalibutan?

Mao kini ang Great Wall of China, Petra, Colosseum, Taj Mahal, Machu Picchu, Christ the Redeemer, ug Chichen Itza!

findings.note: title_bis "Bag-ong Pito Ka Kabanhangan" — "kabanhangan" is not a Cebuano word (single occurrence in the whole sweep corpus); the card's own body and the sibling card ffct-34249 use the correct "Kahibulongan"/"Kabalaghan". Title-only corruption of the wonder term.

fact_en: The Burj Khalifa is about 828 meters (828 m) tall, touching the clouds!
fact_bis: Ang Burj Khalifa mga 828 ka metro (828 m) ang gitas-on, hapit na makakapit sa mga panganod!

findings.note: title_bis "838 Metro si Burj Khalifa" changes the number: EN title and both bodies say 828 m ("mga 828 ka metro (828 m)"). The headline a child sees states a different height than the card; 838 appears nowhere else in the batch.

fact_en:
Is there a highest number on the earthquake magnitude scale?

The earthquake magnitude scale has no fixed highest number; it is open-ended!
fact_bis:
Aduna bay kinatas-ang numero sa magnitude scale sa linog?

Ang magnitude scale sa linog walay gitakdang kinatas-ang numero; abli kini!

findings.note: title_bis "Walay Topas Magnitude" — "topas" is topaz in this corpus (ffct-19042/19369 use topas/topasyo for the gemstone), not "top/highest". Title reads "no topaz magnitude"; the body has the correct wording ("walay gitakdang kinatas-ang numero"), so the title is the outlier.

fact_en:
Did Mount Pinatubo change the Earth's temperature?

Yes! The Earth briefly cooled by about 0.5 °C because of the ash and gas from Mount Pinatubo.
fact_bis:
Nakausab ba ang Pinatubo sa temperatura sa Yuta?

Oo! Ang Yuta temporaryong mibugnaw ug mga 0.5 °C tungod sa abo ug gas nga gibuga sa Pinatubo.

findings.note: title_bis "Pinatubo Nag-uyan" = "Pinatubo rained" (uyan = the l/y-variant of ulan). The English title is "Pinatubo Cooled Earth" and the body correctly says "Ang Yuta temporaryong mibugnaw ug mga 0.5 °C". The title names a different phenomenon (rainfall), which is especially misleading next to the neighbouring Typhoon Yunya / ash-mud card. Suggest "Gipabugnaw sa Pinatubo ang Yuta".

fact_en:
How do we stop soil from washing away on steep slopes?

Planting deep-rooted vetiver grass along the steep slopes of Benguet prevents the topsoil from washing away!
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagsupak sa pag-uwang sa yuta sa mga taluktok nga bukid?

Ang pagtanom og vetiver grass nga adunay lawom nga gamot sa taluktok nga mga bukid sa Benguet makapugong sa topsoil nga ma-uwang!

findings.note: The card's whole subject — soil WASHING AWAY (erosion) — never appears in the Cebuano. EN: "How do we stop soil from washing away on steep slopes? / Planting deep-rooted vetiver grass along the steep slopes of Benguet prevents the topsoil from washing away!" BIS: "Unsaon pagsupak sa pag-uwang sa yuta...? / ...makapugong sa topsoil nga ma-uwang!" In this very corpus 'uwang' is howling/barking (ffct-06105 wolves howl, ffct-08829 'Pag-uwang sa Iro' = why dogs bark, dcard-01641) and the rhinoceros/dung beetle (ffct-08920, ffct-11064); erosion is rendered pag-anod / pagdahili / pagkahugno / maanod everywhere else (ffct-05172, ffct-06557, ffct-02567). A Cebuano-only child reads "stop the soil from howling" and nothing in the card mentions water, rain or washing, so the fact is unrecoverable. Secondary: 'steep slopes' becomes 'taluktok nga bukid' (mountain summits), which also drops the slope.
